models.title: Volume-weighted average price (VWAP)
models.summary: VWAP as total dollar value traded over total quantity; family holds precomputed price-times-quantity per trade.

relationship.original_equation: VWAP = total dollar volume / total number of shares traded
relationship.locator: PDF: LM6 Example 1 Q4, printed p. 419 (PDF p. 429): day dollar volume C$131,230 over 13,000 shares = C$10.0946; fund sales C$100,680 over 10,000 shares = C$10.0680
relationship.translation_notes: Family D holds precomputed pxq per trade (multiplication documented here as the per-element construction; no elementwise family arithmetic in the grammar). Currency/quantity units collapse to currency (unit 1 by pack convention).

variables.source_symbol: price x quantity per trade (introduced family of dollar volumes)
variables.definition: Dollar volume of each trade (price times quantity), in currency units
Total number of shares traded in the set
Volume-weighted average price, in currency units

assumptions: All trades in one consistent set (day benchmark or single order); prices and quantities contemporaneous.
limitations: Equal weighting by value only; VWAP benchmark can equal trade VWAP (bias toward zero) when evaluated trades dominate the benchmark or trade at the market rate (PDF warning).

sources.title: Effective Spreads & VWAP (AnalystPrep CFA Level II notes)
sources.locator: Effective spread cost estimate = Trade size x (Trade price - (Bid+Ask)/2) for buys (reversed for sells); the effective spread is obtained by multiplying by two. Worked buy oracles: X: 6,000x(12.22-12.20) = 120; sell oracles: X: 6,000x(12.225-12.19) = 210, Y: 6,000x(12.225-12.18) = 270. VWAP = sum(Price x Volume)/sum(Volume): 121,060/8,000 = 15.13. VWAP cost estimate = Trade size x (Trade VWAP - VWAP benchmark) for buys (reversed for sells).
sources.evidence: Page states both directional formulas with independent worked oracles reproducing the PDF's forms: per-share effective spreads (buy X: 2x(12.22-12.20) = 0.04), sell costs (X 210, Y 270), VWAP 15.13, and both VWAP cost-estimate branches.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

sources.title: Trading Costs and Electronic Markets (CFA Institute refresher reading)
sources.locator: The bid-ask spread is the difference between the bid and the ask prices. The effective spread is two times the difference between the trade price and the midquote price before the trade occurred. VWAP compares average fill prices to average market prices; implementation shortfall captures all explicit and implicit costs.
sources.evidence: Page states the identical spread definitions (quoted spread as bid-ask difference; effective spread as twice the trade-minus-midquote distance) and the VWAP/implementation-shortfall benchmark roles.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

models.title: VWAP transaction cost estimate for a sell order
models.summary: Sell-side VWAP cost as order size times benchmark VWAP minus trade VWAP.

relationship.original_equation: VWAP transaction cost estimate (sell) = Trade size x (VWAP benchmark - Trade VWAP)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM6 Example 1 Q4, printed p. 419 (PDF p. 429): 10,000 x (C$10.0946 - C$10.0680) = C$266.15 (rounded inputs give C$266.00; exact VWAPs give C$266.15)
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs in currency units, size in shares; output currency (unit 1). Oracle 1 uses exact VWAPs (131230/13000, 100680/10000); tolerance covers the PDF's rounded-input note.

variables.definition: Number of shares in the evaluated order
Benchmark VWAP over the measurement interval, in currency units
Average fill price of the evaluated order, in currency units
Estimated implicit cost, in currency units (negative means the order beat the benchmark)

assumptions: Benchmark interval surrounds the order's fills; trade VWAP from the same fills as the VWAP record.
limitations: Inherits VWAP bias: zero when the order dominates the benchmark regardless of market impact (PDF warning). Positive cost means the sale underperformed the benchmark.

models.title: Average effective spread over a set of fills
models.summary: Mean of per-trade effective spreads; family holds the precomputed per-trade spreads.

relationship.original_equation: Average effective spread = (sum of per-trade effective spreads) / number of trades
relationship.locator: PDF: LM6 Example 1 solutions, printed p. 418 (PDF p. 428): (0.06+0.11+0.22)/3 = 0.13; Q4 solution, printed p. 450 (PDF p. 460): (0.03+0.03+0.06)/3 = 0.04; Q13 solution, printed p. 452 (PDF p. 462): (0.05+0.02)/2 = 0.035
relationship.translation_notes: Family S holds precomputed per-trade effective spreads (buy or sell, computed by sibling records); n is the count. Currency units (unit 1).

variables.definition: Effective spread of each fill, in currency units
Mean effective spread, in currency units

assumptions: All elements are effective spreads of fills of one order (same direction); equal weighting.
limitations: Simple mean over fills, not size-weighted; a large fill counts the same as a small one.
